cards.text: Friend, Jesus just took the little daughter of Jairus, a synagogue leader, by the hand and told her to get up. And she GOT UP (Mark 5:22-23, 41-42). Now Jesus moves on from there, and His disciples come along with Him.

cards.question: Jesus and His disciples are on the move again. Where does Jesus go next?

cards.text: Then the Sabbath comes, and Jesus starts teaching in the synagogue. Hometown crowd, friend, and I bet half that room remembers Him from when He was knee-high. You KNOW somebody in the back is leaning over to whisper, "I know him."

cards.question: Jesus teaches in His hometown synagogue on the Sabbath, and many who hear Him are ___.
The hometown crowd asks where Jesus got these ideas, and how He can perform such miracles.

cards.text: Then the questions get personal. Nothing humbles you like the folks who knew you back when: I came back renewed with a FULL mustache, and I bet the dead batteries I shared that drawer with would STILL call me the dusty stamper.

cards.question: The hometown crowd knows exactly what Jesus did for work. What do they call Him?
The hometown crowd knows Jesus' family too. They call Him the son of ___.

cards.text: Then they run through the whole family tree. His brothers James, Joses, Judas and Simon. And His sisters? Right here in town with them. Friend, that's not a question anymore. That's a ROLL CALL.

cards.question: The hometown crowd is astonished by Jesus' wisdom and miracles, but they know Him as the local carpenter. How do they end up responding to Him?

answers.text: They ask Him to stay longer
They follow Him to the next town

cards.text: Then Jesus speaks to them about how a prophet gets treated. And friend, He doesn't have to look far for an example. He's standing in one.

cards.question: Standing in His hometown, Jesus says a prophet is without honor everywhere he goes.

cards.text: The same Jesus who took a little girl by the hand, and she GOT UP? In His hometown, He could not perform any miracles there. Well... hold on. Except one thing.

cards.question: In His hometown, Jesus could not perform any miracles except one thing. What does He do?

answers.text: He lays hands on a few sick and heals them
He drives demons out of a man in town
He makes a lame man walk at the synagogue

cards.question: Jesus sees the unbelief in His hometown, and He is ___ at it.
After all that unbelief in His hometown, what does Jesus do next?

answers.text: He goes from village to village teaching
He goes up a mountain alone to pray
He sails back across the sea to rest

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 3 quotes "I know him.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Story cards 3, 9, 11 and 13 all exceed two sentences. Only the opening card may run to three sentences; each later story card must be compressed to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Nothing on the earlier cards indicates how the hearers respond to Jesus' teaching. Astonished, unmoved and silent are all compatible with that setup, so the blank asks for an unseen reaction rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: No earlier card names or hints at Jesus' mother. Knowing that the crowd mentions His trade and family does not let the baker reason out Mary rather than Elizabeth or Martha, so this blank depends on prior knowledge or luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The opening clause retells Jesus taking the little girl by the hand and her getting up, which is Mark 5:41-42, but the card cites only Mark 6:5. Its citation is narrower than the Bible content it tells.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The preceding cards do not establish Jesus' emotional response to the unbelief. Amazed, angry and grieved are all plausible reactions to the setup, so the baker cannot reason out the blank from what has been shown.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Cards 2, 7 and 14 already provide several discovery questions whose answers cannot be deduced from the setup. Cards 4, 8 and 15 add three more pure guesses, leaving only four of the ten choice cards as reasoned picks. Discovery questions therefore make up most of the stop rather than the allowed few.

rule.text: Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
